guide.summary: Harvest V3 partner OAuth, production customers (partner acceptance); Custom AI client via Greenhouse MCP server (approval path unconfirmed). Where the path is unconfirmed, the agent did not find it in the provider's docs.
guide.verdict: Harvest V3 partner OAuth, production customers (partner acceptance).

composio.note: Composio lists Greenhouse as managed OAuth. For production, create the auth config with the client ID and secret Greenhouse issues to you, and copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, since Composio's managed app works. For production you will likely want your own app so users see your brand, and Greenhouse only issues credentials to accepted partners.
reasons: Consent screen shows your app name instead of Composio
Dedicated quota instead of quota shared across all Composio users
Control over requested scopes beyond Composio's defaults

prerequisites.title: Mutual customer and public website
prerequisites.detail: The partner request needs at least one mutual customer. You also need an active website with a Privacy Policy.

prerequisites.title: Customers on a paid Greenhouse tier
prerequisites.detail: Harvest API access is tied to Core, Plus or Pro for new subscriptions.

prerequisites.title: Information for the credentials request
prerequisites.detail: Greenhouse needs integration name, environment, scopes, redirect URI(s) and a 128x128 logo.

steps.title: Check partner eligibility
steps.detail: Confirm you have a mutual customer and a live website with a Privacy Policy.

steps.title: Draft request answers and scope list
steps.detail: Draft your integration goals, the minimal Harvest scopes, and the logo spec. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.
steps.done_when: Draft text, scope list and logo requirements are ready.

steps.title: Submit the integration request form
steps.detail: Submit before the first Monday of the month to make that month's review. Submission does not guarantee approval.

steps.title: Wait for monthly partner review
steps.detail: Greenhouse reviews requests monthly and reaches out within 7 business days. Out-of-cycle review is generally only for an urgent mutual customer request.

steps.title: Sign the partnership agreement
steps.detail: A signed agreement is required before credentials are issued.

steps.title: Email Partner Support for credentials
steps.detail: Send integration name, production environment, scopes, redirect URI and logo to partner-support@greenhouse.io.

steps.title: Wait for client ID and secret
steps.detail: Greenhouse issues the Client ID and Client Secret. How long this takes was not found.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API with your own client ID and secret, then store the secret safely.

steps.title: Test the flow and confirm redirect URI
steps.detail: Connect a test account, then tell Greenhouse support the callback works so the final redirect URI is recorded.
steps.done_when: A connected account works and Greenhouse has confirmed the redirect URI.

steps.title: Register client and request allowlisting
steps.detail: Register through Dynamic Client Registration with its own client_id, then contact Greenhouse to allowlist your redirect URI.
steps.done_when: Greenhouse confirms the redirect URI is allowlisted.

steps.title: Ask each customer's Site Admin to enable access
steps.detail: The Site Admin enables data categories under Dev Center > MCP Access before users can authorize.
steps.done_when: Users see your categories on the consent screen.

traps.title: Partner acceptance can be refused
traps.detail: Not all submissions are accepted, and the form is not a confirmation. Plan for no credentials at all.

traps.title: Monthly review cycle
traps.detail: Requests are reviewed only once a month, so missing the cutoff costs about a month.

traps.title: Refresh token expires after 14 days unused
traps.detail: Users must redo the whole authorization if the refresh token is unused for 14 days. Access tokens last 1 hour.

traps.title: Authorization code lasts 1 minute
traps.detail: Exchange the code immediately on the server.

traps.title: Redirect URI must match exactly
traps.detail: The redirect URI in each request must match the one registered with your client ID.

traps.title: Testing is sandbox only
traps.detail: A testing-environment app only reaches your own sandbox, not customers.

traps.title: Managed app shows Composio branding
traps.detail: Users see Composio on the consent screen, the most common reason to switch to your own app.

traps.title: Per-user tokens required
traps.detail: Greenhouse vets for a separate OAuth token per user and rejects shared credentials.

blockers.symptom: invalid_scope error or 401 on token exchange
blockers.what_it_means: You requested scopes not permitted for your client application.
blockers.what_to_do: Request only scopes you declared to Greenhouse, or ask Partner Support to add them.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare requested scopes with the declared list.

blockers.symptom: Partner request declined or no reply
blockers.what_it_means: Greenhouse did not accept the integration into the program.
blockers.what_to_do: Use Composio's managed app meanwhile and ask the Partnerships team what to change.

evidence.answer: A toolkit is listed under 'Composio-managed OAuth available' when Composio manages at least one OAuth method for it.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio can provide the OAuth app that your users authorize when they connect a toolkit. You do not need to register an OAuth app or supply its client ID and client secret.
evidence.answer: Composio can provide the OAuth app that users authorize when they connect a toolkit, so the developer does not need to register an OAuth app or supply a client ID and secret for managed toolkits.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Open the toolkit page to check each method.
evidence.answer: Some toolkits support more than one authentication method, so each method should be checked on the toolkit page.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: If `composio_managed_auth_schemes` contains the toolkit's OAuth method, Composio provides the OAuth app. If the field does not contain that method, register your own OAuth app and supply its client ID and client secret.
evidence.answer: If the toolkit's OAuth method appears in composio_managed_auth_schemes, Composio provides the OAuth app; otherwise the developer must register their own OAuth app and supply its client ID and client secret.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: To get started, you must have a signed Greenhouse partnership agreement.
evidence.answer: A signed Greenhouse partnership agreement is required before a developer can start the OAuth setup.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Once the agreement is finalized, you can proceed with the steps below.
evidence.answer: The steps are only meant to be followed once the partnership agreement is finalized.

evidence.question: G1
evidence.quote: Use the stored access_token to make calls to the Greenhouse Harvest V3 API.
evidence.answer: The page covers OAuth for the Greenhouse Harvest V3 API.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Before you start, you need API credentials from Greenhouse.
evidence.answer: Before starting, a developer must get API credentials from Greenhouse, which are issued on request rather than self-registered.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Greenhouse will provide you with a Client ID and a Client Secret . Keep your Client Secret confidential!
evidence.answer: Greenhouse issues the Client ID and Client Secret to the developer.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Environment: Is this for testing (only your own sandbox) or production (live for mutual customers)?
evidence.answer: The developer must choose whether the integration is for testing (only their own sandbox) or production (live for mutual customers).

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Once your callback endpoint ( redirect_uri ) is operational and tested, please inform Greenhouse support via
evidence.answer: After the callback endpoint is working and tested, the developer must inform Greenhouse support so that the final redirect URI is recorded.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Provide Information: Tell us:
evidence.answer: To obtain credentials, the developer must send Greenhouse partner support the integration name, environment, required scopes, redirect URI(s), and a logo.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Integration Name: What is your product/integration called?
evidence.answer: The request requires the integration's product or integration name.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Logo: Provide a 128x128 logo file. Customers will see this when authorizing your integration.
evidence.answer: The request requires a 128x128 logo file, which customers see when authorizing the integration.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Required Scopes: Which specific data permissions does your integration need (e.g., harvest:job_posts:list , harvest:candidates:list )? See Harvest API documentation for available scopes.
evidence.answer: The developer declares which data permissions (scopes) the integration needs; examples given are harvest:job_posts:list and harvest:candidates:list, with the full list in the Harvest API documentation.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: scope=<SCOPES> (Required: A space-separated list of the permissions you need, e.g., harvest:job_posts:list harvest:candidates:list )
evidence.answer: Scopes are requested as a space-separated list in the authorization request.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: (You requested scopes not permitted for your client application).
evidence.answer: Requesting scopes not permitted for the client application produces an invalid_scope error.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: This occurs if the client tries to exchange a code associated with scopes it isn't permitted to request.
evidence.answer: A token exchange fails with HTTP 401 if the client tries to exchange a code tied to scopes it is not permitted to request.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Environment: Is this for testing (only your own sandbox) or production (live for mutual customers)?
evidence.answer: A testing environment is limited to the developer's own sandbox, while production is live for mutual customers.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Authorization Code: 1 minute (Must be exchanged quickly!)
evidence.answer: The authorization code lasts 1 minute and must be exchanged quickly.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Access Token: 1 hour (Used to make API calls)
evidence.answer: The access token lasts 1 hour and is used to make API calls.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Refresh Token: 14 days (Used to get new access tokens)
evidence.answer: The refresh token lasts 14 days and is used to get new access tokens.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: IMPORTANT: You have only 1 minute to exchange the code before it expires!
evidence.answer: The developer has only 1 minute to exchange the code before it expires.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: IMPORTANT: If the refresh_token expires (not used within 14 days), the user must repeat the entire authorization flow from Step 2.
evidence.answer: If the refresh token is not used within 14 days, it expires and the user must repeat the whole authorization flow.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Redirect URI(s): The url(s) where you handle the authorization code callback (see step 3)
evidence.answer: The redirect URI is the URL where the developer handles the authorization code callback, and it must be provided to Greenhouse.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Must match the one registered with your client_id .
evidence.answer: The redirect_uri sent in the authorization request must match the one registered with the client ID.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: (The provided redirect_uri doesn't match the one registered for your client_id ).
evidence.answer: If the redirect_uri does not match the one registered for the client ID, Greenhouse returns an invalid_request error with HTTP 400.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Build the Authorization URL: Link your button to the Greenhouse authorization endpoint: https://auth.greenhouse.io/authorize
evidence.answer: The developer links the Connect button to the Greenhouse authorization endpoint at https://auth.greenhouse.io/authorize.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Combine your Client ID and Client Secret with a colon ( : ), like your_client_id_123:your_client_secret_xyz . Then, Base64 encode this entire string.
evidence.answer: For token exchange, the developer combines the Client ID and Client Secret with a colon and Base64-encodes the result for the Authorization header.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Make a POST Request: Immediately send a server-to-server POST request to the Greenhouse token endpoint: https://auth.greenhouse.io/token
evidence.answer: The token exchange is a server-to-server POST request to https://auth.greenhouse.io/token.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: (Optional: If you need Greenhouse logos or branding guidelines, please consult https://brand.greenhouse.io )
evidence.answer: Greenhouse logos and branding guidelines are available at a brand site, for optional use.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: During OAuth, the browser briefly redirects through `backend.composio.dev` so Composio can capture the auth token.
evidence.answer: During OAuth, the browser briefly redirects through Composio's backend.composio.dev domain so Composio can capture the auth token.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Some toolkits also display this URL on the consent screen.
evidence.answer: Some toolkits also display Composio's backend URL on the consent screen.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: If you need to hide Composio's domain, you can proxy the redirect through your own domain instead.
evidence.answer: To hide Composio's domain, you can proxy the redirect through your own domain instead.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: In your OAuth app's settings, set the authorized redirect URI to your own endpoint:
evidence.answer: When proxying, you set the authorized redirect URI in your OAuth app's settings to your own endpoint.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: https://yourdomain.com/api/composio-redirect
evidence.answer: The example proxy redirect URI is https://yourdomain.com/api/composio-redirect.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: This endpoint receives the OAuth callback and immediately 302-redirects it to Composio:
evidence.answer: The proxy endpoint receives the OAuth callback and immediately sends a 302 redirect to Composio's callback URL.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Your endpoint must return a **302 redirect**. Do not follow the redirect server-side or make a fetch call to Composio. The user's browser needs to be redirected so the OAuth flow completes correctly.
evidence.answer: The proxy endpoint must return a 302 redirect, not follow the redirect server-side or make a fetch call to Composio, so the user's browser is redirected.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback
evidence.answer: The Composio callback target used by the proxy is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Add your own OAuth app only for toolkits where the provider consent screen must show your brand.
evidence.answer: Composio's documentation says to add your own OAuth app only for toolkits where the provider consent screen must show your brand.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: "Composio wants to access your account" on Google, GitHub, etc.
evidence.answer: Without your own OAuth app, the provider's consent screen shows 'Composio wants to access your account' on Google, GitHub, etc.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Use your own OAuth app
evidence.answer: The documented fix for the Composio-branded consent screen is to use your own OAuth app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Set your app title, logo, and theme for the hosted Connect Link.
evidence.answer: The hosted Connect Link shows Composio's logo, name and styling by default, which you can change by setting your logo, app title, and theme in the dashboard.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio-branded success page after OAuth completes
evidence.answer: The post-auth success page is Composio-branded after OAuth completes, unless you pass a callbackUrl when initiating the connection.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio registers and maintains OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack. You do not need to register your own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: Composio registers and maintains its own OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack, so you do not need to register your own OAuth app for those (the page does not name Greenhouse).

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed apps are the default when they are available.
evidence.answer: Managed apps are the default when they are available.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: To check whether Composio provides the OAuth app for a toolkit, see [Managed OAuth apps](/toolkits/managed-auth).
evidence.answer: To check whether Composio provides the OAuth app for a given toolkit, consult the Managed OAuth apps page.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed apps share quota across all Composio users.
evidence.answer: Composio's managed apps share quota across all Composio users.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Your own app gets a dedicated quota.
evidence.answer: A developer's own OAuth app gets a dedicated quota, unlike the shared managed app quota.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval; your own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.
evidence.answer: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval for triggers; a developer's own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio requests sensible defaults for each toolkit.
evidence.answer: Composio requests sensible default scopes for each toolkit under managed apps, and these defaults may not include everything a developer needs.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio's default scopes may not include everything you need (e.g., write access to a specific Google API).
evidence.answer: Composio's default scopes may not include everything needed, for example write access to a specific Google API.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Users will see "Composio wants to access your account" during OAuth.
evidence.answer: With managed apps, users see a consent screen saying Composio wants access to their account during OAuth.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: In production, users should see your app name, not "Composio." This is the most common reason to switch.
evidence.answer: In production, users should see the developer's app name rather than Composio on OAuth consent screens, which is the most common reason to switch to a custom app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You provide your own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials and tell Composio to use them for a toolkit.
evidence.answer: Custom auth configs let a developer supply their own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials for a toolkit.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Use your own credentials for toolkits where users see consent screens (GitHub, Google, Slack) and Composio managed auth for the rest. Each toolkit gets its own auth config independently.
evidence.answer: A developer may mix approaches: own credentials for toolkits with user-facing consent screens and Composio managed auth for the rest, with each toolkit getting its own auth config.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: **You're connecting to a custom instance.** Self-hosted or regional variants (e.g., a private Salesforce subdomain) need their own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: Self-hosted or regional variants of a toolkit, such as a private Salesforce subdomain, need their own OAuth app rather than the managed one.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: The AI tool registers using OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration and receives a client_id
evidence.answer: For the Greenhouse MCP server, an AI tool registers itself through OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration and receives a client_id.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: There is no client secret because the tool is treated as a public client.
evidence.answer: For the Greenhouse MCP server, the registered tool is treated as a public client, so no client secret is issued.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: The list is not fixed.
evidence.answer: Greenhouse keeps a global list of supported AI tools, and the page says the list is not fixed.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Any tool that implements the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE and Dynamic Client Registration can request to be added.
evidence.answer: Any AI tool implementing OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code with PKCE and Dynamic Client Registration can ask Greenhouse to be added to the supported list.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: Currently, we vet against two requirements for our global list of supported tools, and neither is negotiable:
evidence.answer: Greenhouse vets tools for its global supported list against two requirements, and neither is negotiable.

evidence.question: G2
evidence.quote: To add one, contact Greenhouse to have its redirect URI added to the allowlist. This is a manual step today.
evidence.answer: Custom or internal MCP clients need Greenhouse to add their redirect URI to the allowlist by a manual step, which the page says is a manual step today.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: The tool must obtain a separate OAuth token for each individual user.
evidence.answer: Greenhouse vets a tool for per-user authorization, requiring a separate OAuth token for each individual user.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: Shared credentials are rejected, so every action stays traceable to the specific person who authorized it.
evidence.answer: Shared credentials are rejected when vetting tools for the Greenhouse MCP supported list.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: The tool’s callback URL must be registered and checked against Greenhouse’s allowlist every time a user authorizes, not just once at registration.
evidence.answer: Greenhouse checks a tool's callback URL against its allowlist every time a user authorizes, not only at registration.

evidence.question: G3
evidence.quote: This check is designed to reduce the risk of authorization codes being intercepted.
evidence.answer: The redirect URI check is designed to reduce the risk of authorization codes being intercepted.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: Site Admins choose which Harvest API endpoint categories are available to MCP tools, and whether each one is read, write, or both.
evidence.answer: Site Admins choose which Harvest API endpoint categories MCP tools can use, and whether each is read, write, or both.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: To make MCP read-only, enable only the read scopes.
evidence.answer: To make the Greenhouse MCP server read-only, a Site Admin enables only the read scopes.

evidence.question: G4
evidence.quote: The MCP Access page is the best source of truth for the API scopes that are available to the MCP server.
evidence.answer: The MCP Access page in Dev Center is the best source of truth for which API scopes are available to the Greenhouse MCP server.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Access tokens expire after one hour.
evidence.answer: For the Greenhouse MCP server, access tokens expire after one hour.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: In most cases they refresh automatically, though the exact behavior depends on your AI client or proxy implementation.
evidence.answer: Access tokens usually refresh automatically, though behavior depends on the AI client or proxy implementation.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Refresh tokens remain valid until there have been 14 consecutive days of inactivity.
evidence.answer: Refresh tokens stay valid until 14 consecutive days of inactivity, after which the user must re-authorize the AI tool.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Every request through MCP is permission-bound, scoped by OAuth, rate-limited, and non-persistent on the Greenhouse side, so there is a hard limit on what any single call can reach.
evidence.answer: Every MCP request is rate-limited on the Greenhouse side, though the page gives no specific rate numbers.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: The data categories your Site Admin has enabled in Dev Center > MCP Access
evidence.answer: Customer access to the Greenhouse MCP server is limited to the data categories a Site Admin has enabled in Dev Center > MCP Access.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: After signing in, you see a consent screen listing the data categories the tool is requesting, limited by what your organization has enabled.
evidence.answer: When a user connects an AI tool, a consent screen lists the data categories the tool requests, limited by what the organization has enabled.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: No access is granted until you approve.
evidence.answer: No access is granted to the AI tool until the user approves on the consent screen.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Users will need to re-authorize under the new configuration.
evidence.answer: When Site Admins change MCP scopes, affected users must re-authorize under the new configuration.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Greenhouse MCP uses the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE).
evidence.answer: The Greenhouse MCP server uses the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: All communication with the Greenhouse MCP server is encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher.
evidence.answer: All communication with the Greenhouse MCP server is encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: The tool’s callback URL must be registered and checked against Greenhouse’s allowlist every time a user authorizes, not just once at registration.
evidence.answer: The page does not describe domain ownership verification or authorized domain rules; redirect URIs are checked against Greenhouse's allowlist.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Site Admin: In Greenhouse Recruiting, go to Dev Center > MCP Access
evidence.answer: Site Admins configure MCP scopes in Greenhouse Recruiting under Dev Center > MCP Access.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Organization-specific management of redirect URLs is planned for a future release, which would allow organization-specific governance for approved AI tools that can interact with the Greenhouse MCP server.
evidence.answer: Organization-specific management of redirect URLs is planned for a future release and is not available yet.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Yes. Any AI tool or custom application that implements the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE and Dynamic Client Registration can connect to the Greenhouse MCP server.
evidence.answer: Any AI tool or custom application implementing OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code with PKCE and Dynamic Client Registration can connect to the Greenhouse MCP server.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Greenhouse currently supports Claude (Anthropic), ChatGPT (OpenAI), Microsoft Copilot Studio, Glean, Amazon Q, and Grok.
evidence.answer: Greenhouse currently lists Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Glean, Amazon Q, and Grok as supported AI tools.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Custom clients go through the same registration and authorization flow and are held to the same per-user permission enforcement.
evidence.answer: Custom clients must go through the same registration and authorization flow and face the same per-user permission enforcement.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: so register your client with its own distinct client_id . Do not reuse one across multiple users or contexts.
evidence.answer: Each custom client should register its own distinct client_id and must not reuse one across multiple users or contexts.

evidence.question: G7
evidence.quote: Product tier: Available for new subscription tiers (Core, Plus, and Pro)
evidence.answer: Harvest API access is tied to Greenhouse Recruiting subscription tiers (Core, Plus, Pro) for new subscriptions, so customers need a qualifying paid Greenhouse plan; no separate API fee or credit charge is stated on this page.
